hook: Your phone use at night is doing more damage than your phone use during the day.
topic: Night-time stimulation, sleep stages, and dopamine sensitivity restoration
body:
**Your phone use at night is doing more damage than your phone use during the day.**

Here's why. Dopamine sensitivity — your brain's ability to register normal rewards as rewarding — is partially restored during sleep. Specifically, during the deep sleep stages in the first half of the night. High-stimulation input before bed delays sleep onset, shortens those early deep sleep cycles, and interrupts the restoration process.

This means the recalibration that should happen overnight doesn't fully complete. You wake up with a sensitivity deficit already in place. The threshold is elevated before the day begins. You reach for the phone first thing not just from habit, but because your brain is already operating below its natural baseline.

Night-time phone use is a compounding variable. It doesn't just affect the evening. It affects the entire next day — the focus window, the tolerance for hard work, the pull toward low-effort inputs. Every hour of late-screen exposure costs you more than that hour.

The single highest-leverage change in a reset protocol is screens off 90 minutes before sleep. Not because of blue light. Because of stimulus load.

Full protocol in the link in bio.
